mechanism_narrative: Persistent elevated residential mobility reflects a continued preference for staying home and reduced out-of-home activities, directly reducing discretionary trips to retail and recreation venues, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining elevated above 7% change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If workplace mobility shows any further week-on-week increase from its current stable level, it signals a gradual return to office-based routines, which will incrementally boost local retail and recreation activity, resulting in higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES increases by more than 1 point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: As the holiday season approaches, a stable level of grocery and pharmacy visits combined with a slight recovery in parks activity suggests people are venturing out more for essential and limited leisure, which will translate into a modest increase in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable (within +/- 1 point) and PARKS not falling below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: If new public health restrictions are announced or implied by local authorities, the already low transit station activity will further deter non-essential travel and shopping, causing a sharp decline in retail and recreation mobility over the next week.
candidate_trigger: Announcement of new public health restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite new restrictions being implemented.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently low levels of transit station mobility indicate a sustained reduction in public transport usage for commuting and leisure, which will continue to suppress overall retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks due to reduced accessibility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT remaining at or below -25% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in parks mobility, exceeding its t-3w level of -5.3%, would indicate increased comfort with outdoor activities and a general willingness to leave home, which will positively impact retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if PARKS mobility recovers significantly above -5.3%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of persistently high residential mobility and low workplace attendance creates a strong and reinforcing disincentive for discretionary retail and recreation trips, leading to a continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 7% and WORKPLACES remaining below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: As winter weather sets in around mid-December, the seasonal reduction in outdoor activities, as evidenced by the recent dip in parks mobility, will generally reduce overall foot traffic and discretionary spending, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite PARKS mobility remaining below -15% due to seasonal factors.
